_comment: ECS Fargate task definition for pnsm-ai-svc (Person 4, Quadrant IV).
Placeholders in ANGLE BRACKETS are filled by scripts/provision_aws.py, which
renders this file with the account id, region and ARNs it just created.
Nothing here is a secret: every secret arrives through `secrets`, which ECS
resolves from Secrets Manager at task start. A secret in `environment` would
be visible to anyone with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition, which is a wider
Sizing: 0.5 vCPU / 1024 MB. Two ONNX sessions plus the Python runtime sit
around 300 MB resident (tests/memory enforces the ceiling); 1024 MB is the
smallest Fargate memory value that pairs with 512 CPU units and leaves room
for a burst without the kernel OOM-killing a check-in mid-inference.
This file describes the AI service only. Person 3's Express API and the two
nginx frontends get their own task definitions from the same template; the
differences are the image, port, health-check path and secret list.
_comment_roles: executionRoleArn pulls the image and writes log streams -- it is used by
the ECS agent BEFORE the container runs, and is also what reads the
taskRoleArn is what the application code itself gets: KMS and S3, nothing
else. Keeping them separate is OWASP A01 at the infrastructure layer -- a
compromised container cannot pull other images or read other secrets.

containerDefinitions.name: ai-svc
_comment_hardening: readonlyRootFilesystem is the single highest-value container control
here: the service writes nothing to disk at runtime, so a file dropped
by an exploit has nowhere to land. /tmp is mounted as a tmpfs volume
below because Python's tempfile and ONNX Runtime both expect it.
The image already runs as uid 10001; `user` restates it so a rebuilt
image that lost its USER directive cannot silently start as root.
_comment_secrets: PNSM_FLE_KEYS is still listed even though PNSM_KEY_PROVIDER=kms. It is
not used to seal anything new: it is what opens envelopes written
before the KMS migration, so `scripts/rotate_keys.py --to kms` can
re-wrap them. Remove this entry once the migration report shows zero
_comment_health: startPeriod 60s covers the cold start: interpreter, two ONNX sessions
and one warm-up inference. Without it the first probe fires while the
model is still loading and ECS kills a task that was about to be fine.
/health is deliberately cheap -- no model call, no network -- so the
probe never competes with a check-in for the half-core it has.

_comment_volumes: An empty `host` volume, not EBS or EFS. On Fargate that is a scratch
directory on the task's own ephemeral storage: AWS encrypts it at rest,
and it is destroyed with the task, so nothing written under /tmp outlives
the container or reaches a volume another task could mount.
Note that Fargate does NOT support linuxParameters.tmpfs -- that field is
EC2-launch-type only, and a task definition using it is rejected at
registration. This is the Fargate-legal equivalent.
